ChatClientPersistence.reason: Dart adapters return Object? at the boundary, but ChatPersistor rejects legacy bare arrays and protects them from writes until cleared; stored records use ChatPersistedState.

ChatPersistenceOptions.reason: Named ephemeral, server and stored choices carry storage/history only; the client constructor requires the thread ID once.

ChatPersistenceOption.reason: The modern constructor accepts ChatPersistenceOptions named variants. Explicit legacy constructors additionally retain the older bool or adapter call shape.

ChatClientSnapshot.reason: Dart publishes ChatSnapshot with enum states, immutable interrupt state and an additional resumeState pointer for the atomic states stream.

ChatTransport.reason: Dart uses named ConnectionAdapter variants and fetcherToConnectionAdapter for the modern contract; ChatTransport remains an explicit legacy stream seam.

ChatRequestBody.reason: Modern adapters build the canonical RunAgentInput JSON map with required thread and run identity, resume entries and forwardedProps.

GenerationFetcherOptions.reason: Dart uses CancellationSignal and requires threadId and runId on the typed fetcher options, with optional BYOK headers.

RunAgentInputContext.reason: Dart named fields require threadId and runId; adapter connect and send callbacks require this value.

ByokProviderInit.reason: The provider initializer is declared by the @tanstack/ai/byok server package; the Dart client exposes ByokProvider and defineByokProvider instead.
